entries.title: Burmese at a glance
body: Burmese is the official language of Myanmar, spoken by about 33 million people as a first language and by many more as a second. It belongs to the Sino-Tibetan family, together with Tibetan and the Chinese languages.

The verb comes last, and small particles after nouns and verbs do the work of grammar: a sentence ends with တယ် for the present or past, မယ် for the future, and ဘူး after a verb marked with မ for “not”. Words never change form.
Burmese is tonal, and the written language (used in books and news) differs from the spoken language in many common particles.

examples.t: ကျွန်တော် မြန်မာစကား သင်နေ{တယ်}။
examples.r: Kyanaw Myanma zaga thin ne de.

entries.title: How Burmese script works
body: Burmese script comes from the Brahmi family of India, by way of the Mon script. Its letters are built mostly from circles and parts of circles. Each consonant carries an inherent a sound, and vowel marks above, below, before or after the consonant change it.
Words are not separated by spaces; spaces fall between phrases. The ၊ mark works like a comma and ။ ends a sentence.

head: Written
Sound
Example
rows: the ် mark silences the inherent vowel

entries.title: Tones
body: Burmese has three main tones, plus a short syllable that ends in a stop. The tone is shown in writing with marks such as း (high) and ့ (creaky).

entries.title: Sentence endings
entries.body: Verbs do not change; endings after the verb show time, negation and questions.

head: Ending
Meaning
Example
rows: သွားတယ်, I go / I went
သွားမယ်, I will go
သွားနေတယ်, I am going
သွားပြီ, I'm off now
မသွားဘူး, I don't go
သွားမလား, will you go?
ထိုင်ပါ, please sit

entries.title: Classifiers
entries.body: Counting uses noun, then number, then classifier: ကော်ဖီ နှစ်ခွက်, two (cups of) coffee.

head: Classifier
Used for
Example
rows: လူ သုံးယောက်, three people
ခွေး တစ်ကောင်, one dog
စာအုပ် နှစ်အုပ်, two books
ရေ တစ်ခွက်, a glass of water
နှစ်ခု, two things
ကား တစ်စီး, one car

entries.title: Numbers and Burmese digits
entries.body: Burmese has its own digits, used on signs, prices and bus numbers alongside the ones used in English. Before ဆယ် (ten), ရာ (hundred) and ထောင် (thousand), တစ် is said ta and နှစ် is said hna.

examples.t: ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်
ဒါ ဘယ်လောက်လဲ
နားမလည်ဘူး

entries.title: Names and titles
body: Most people in Myanmar have no family name. A name is one to four syllables chosen for the person, often linked to the day of the week they were born on.

A title goes before the name and shows age and respect: ဦး (U) for an older man, ဒေါ် (Daw) for an older woman, ကို (Ko) for a young man, and မ (Ma) for a young woman. Aung San Suu Kyi is Daw Aung San Suu Kyi.
